evidence.note: Apply/Fold/FoldFull checked clause-by-clause against docs/specs/2026-08-26-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-run-persistence.md sections 4.1-4.9: init field copy, node_output last-wins, delta_applied hash+status coverage, llm_call index, tree, transition loop/outcome, fix_baseline order, terminal set, provenance and stamps all match the spec text.

withinCaps cross-checked against the section 2.3 cap table: MaxShort/MaxText/MaxDesc/MaxDetail/MaxStderr and every count cap (Vars 64, Goldens 64, AllowedCmds 16, Argv 32, FileHashes 64, delta lists 256, Warnings 1024) are all enforced; the payload types with no case (NodeOutputData, EmptyData, TokenTotals) are bounded by MaxPayload or by the explicit Negative/TooLarge checks in Apply.

cow() clones every reference-typed Snapshot field that Apply can write (Vars, Lineage, AllowedCmds, Goldens, Findings, Confirmed, AllFound, Status, PrevUnfixed, NodeOutputs, Applied, NodesRun, LastError, Warnings, indexes), so the documented purity of Apply holds; nil-vs-empty normalisation is consistent with applyInit, keeping the canonical snapshot encoding deterministic.

Token accumulation cannot overflow int64: Apply rejects any record with a counter above MaxTokenCounter (2^40, types.go:112) and the store caps counted events at DefaultMaxEvents (100000, store.go:163), bounding the sum near 1.1e17.

FSSidecar.Write uses O_WRONLY|O_CREATE|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW at 0600 and FSSidecar.Read uses O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW with a MaxPayload+1 LimitReader, so symlink, clobber and unbounded-read paths are all closed; ValidSidecarName's regexp rejects path separators, dotfiles, 'lock' and every 'audit.' name, matching the spec 2 M9 row.

Validation evidence for sidecar.go: the M9 block asserts symlink refusal on read and write, exists, missing run dir, bad run id, reserved name, too_large, List filtering/order, 0600 mode, unreadable file, and injected write/close/read failures; MemSidecar edge rows follow at 1425.

The +2 buffer arithmetic is correct: bufio.Scanner errors when len(buf) >= maxTokenSize and ScanLines needs the terminator inside the buffer, so max+2 admits a line of exactly maxJSONLLineBytes ending in CRLF. runchain_test.go:254 pins that exact-length case.

Executed the script directly: 'test-override: ok'. It is wired into the suite at tests/run-all.sh:26, and the 'grep -q ... && fail' negative assertions are safe under set -e because a failing non-final command in an AND list does not trigger the shell's exit (verified empirically).

Validation evidence: go test ./internal/fsm/run/ and ./internal/fsm/machine/ both pass at 100.0% statement coverage; ./internal/runchain/ passes at 89.7% with the new line-cap row covered by runchain_test.go:254. No TODO/FIXME markers, no eval, and no unsafe execution in any of the four shard files.

findings.note: Apply never validates ev.Origin on the init event. The TypeInit branch at internal/fsm/run/fold.go:58 returns before checkProvenance (fold.go:423) is reached, so spec section 4.8's rule 'no Origin outside seqs 2..ForkedAtSeq' is unenforced at seq 1: an init line carrying a fabricated Origin folds cleanly. Not reachable in-tree - fork.go:222 builds the child's init with no Origin - so this is a defence-in-depth gap in the fold's fail-closed contract rather than an exploitable path.

evidence.note: init returns early, so checkProvenance at fold.go:423 never runs for seq 1.
The child's init event is constructed without an Origin, which is why the gap is unreachable in-tree.

findings.note: The envelope cap check at internal/fsm/run/fold.go:43 measures ev.Type, ev.Node and ev.State against MaxShort but not ev.Origin.RunID or ev.Origin.Hash, both of which the section 2.3 table classifies as MaxShort ('ids', 'hashes'). internal/fsm/run/store.go:152 justifies the absence of any MaxLine check with 'MaxLine is always satisfied once Apply has enforced MaxPayload and the MaxShort envelope caps', so that justification is incomplete: a caller-supplied Origin is unbounded. Producers in-tree write a 64-hex hash and a validated run id, so no oversized line can actually be written today.

evidence.note: Envelope cap check omits ev.Origin.RunID and ev.Origin.Hash.
Comment asserts MaxLine needs no check because Apply enforces the MaxShort envelope caps.

findings.note: FSSidecar.List maps every os.ReadDir failure to reason 'missing' (internal/fsm/machine/sidecar.go:111-113), including EACCES and ENOTDIR. Write and Read in the same file take care to separate 'missing'/'exists' from 'path', so a caller keying off errs.Field("reason") is told a permission failure is an absent run. Cosmetic today because the only consumers surface ERR_SIDECAR wholesale.

evidence.note: Every ReadDir error becomes sidecarErr("missing", ...) regardless of cause.
Read distinguishes fs.ErrNotExist ('missing') from any other open error ('path'), the behaviour List departs from.

findings.note: MemSidecar.WriteErr is read at internal/fsm/machine/sidecar.go:140 before m.mu is taken at line 143, while every other method reads and writes state under the mutex. Tests set the field between calls today (fork_test.go:877), so no race exists yet, but the seam is exported on a type whose whole point is being shared, and a -race run that ever sets it from another goroutine would flag it.

evidence.note: WriteErr is read outside the mutex that guards the rest of MemSidecar's state.

findings.note: Two readers of the same .metareview/runs.jsonl now disagree on the maximum readable line by two bytes: internal/runchain/runchain.go:114 (and state.go:66, findings.go:488, reviewlog.go:290) pass maxJSONLLineBytes+2, while internal/fsm/record/record.go:156 passes 1<<20 exactly. A row in the 1048576..1048577 byte window is therefore readable by ReadRuns but makes record.readRows fail with bufio.ErrTooLong, and since appendRow calls readRows first, every later FSM terminal-row append would fail on a file the other gates read fine. The window is narrow and no in-tree writer approaches it, but the two callers should share one constant.

evidence.note: scanner.Buffer(..., maxJSONLLineBytes+2) admits a 1 MiB line.
sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 1<<20), 1<<20) on the same runs.jsonl file rejects it.

findings.note: The read cap is raised without a matching write cap, and the constant is duplicated verbatim (identical three-line comment included) in four packages. state.AppendJSONL (internal/state/state.go:28-50) marshals and appends a record of any size, so an oversized row still makes ReadRuns fail hard for every later invocation rather than being skipped or truncated. The change is a strict improvement over the 64 KiB default and runchain.Record has no plausibly unbounded field, so this is a durability note rather than a defect in the diff.

evidence.note: AppendJSONL applies no size limit to the marshalled record before writing the line.
maxJSONLLineBytes and its comment are copied into state.go:17, findings.go:15 and reviewlog.go:17 as well.
